title: L&T Wins Major Dhaka Metro Line 1 Systems Contracts in Bangladesh
excerpt: L&T's Transportation Infrastructure business will deliver track and electrical systems with Sumitomo under CP09, and signalling, telecommunications and platform screen doors under CP10, for Bangladesh's first underground metro.
body:
• Larsen & Toubro's Transportation Infrastructure business has won major design-and-build orders for two systems packages of Dhaka Metro Line 1, awarded by Dhaka Mass Transit Company Limited.
  • Package CP09 covers track works and electrical systems, with Japan's Sumitomo Corporation as partner, while CP10 covers signalling, telecommunications and platform screen doors.
  • Under L&T's order classification, a major order is valued between Rs 5,000 crore and Rs 10,000 crore, according to NBMCW.
  • Line 1, funded by the Japan International Cooperation Agency, will span about 31 km with 19 stations and a depot at Pitalganj, as Bangladesh's first underground metro.

Larsen & Toubro has secured major design-and-build orders for Dhaka Metro Line 1 in Bangladesh, adding a repeat win with Dhaka Mass Transit Company Limited to the Indian engineering company's overseas urban transit work. The contracts cover the core systems that allow a metro line to run: track, power, signalling, telecommunications and platform screen doors.

The orders were awarded to L&T's Transportation Infrastructure business for the Dhaka Mass Rapid Transit Development Project, Line 1, described by both NBMCW and InfraInsiders as the country's first underground metro project. L&T did not disclose a package-wise value in the InfraInsiders report, while NBMCW noted that under L&T's own order classification, major orders are valued between Rs 5,000 crore and Rs 10,000 crore.

Two Packages, Two Different Jobs

Under Contract Package CP09, L&T will work with Japanese partner Sumitomo Corporation to design, procure, install, test and commission track works and electrical infrastructure across the corridor. That package includes power supply and distribution systems, traction substations, overhead catenary systems and associated electrical facilities.

https://x.com/SwarajyaMag/status/2115020729498685680

Under Contract Package CP10, L&T will execute signalling, telecommunications and platform screen door systems across the network. Those systems support train operations, operational communications and passenger safety at stations. Together, the two packages cover key systems required to operate the line, rather than civil construction of tunnels or stations.

"The repeat orders from Dhaka Mass Transit Company Limited (DMTCL) are a testament to L&T's capabilities in delivering large scale, integrated urban transit projects globally."

— Ramkumar S, Senior Vice President & Head, Transportation Infrastructure, L&T

The Line L&T Will Help Equip

Dhaka Metro Line 1 will extend approximately 31 kilometres across two routes, funded by the Japan International Cooperation Agency, known as JICA. The Airport Route will connect Kamalapur with the Airport, while the Purbachal Route will run from Natun Bazar to Purbachal Terminal. The project includes 19 stations and a depot at Pitalganj, according to both reports.

For Dhaka, the significance is the underground format. Line 1 is planned as Bangladesh's first underground metro system, a step beyond the elevated corridor already in operation. The systems packages are therefore central to delivery: without track, traction power, signalling and platform screen doors, the civil works cannot become a working railway.

A Repeat Customer in Dhaka

L&T is not new to Dhaka's metro program. NBMCW reported that Ramkumar S pointed to a strong track record of delivering electrical and mechanical systems for Dhaka Metro Line 6, and more recently work on the Jakarta Metro, which is under execution. InfraInsiders made the same connection, noting that L&T previously delivered the integrated railway systems package for Dhaka Metro Line 6, Bangladesh's first metro corridor, which is now operational, and is also executing an electrical and mechanical systems package for the Jakarta Metro.

That history helps explain the wording in L&T's statement. Repeat orders from the same transit authority signal that a previous systems delivery was accepted, and that the client is willing to place a more complex underground program with the same contractor. For an Indian company competing alongside a Japanese partner, and on a project funded by a Japanese agency, the win also shows how South Asian metro work is assembled through international consortia rather than single-country bids.

What This Means Beyond Bangladesh

For readers following Indian companies abroad, the contract is a concrete example of engineering exports: an Indian firm selling design, procurement, installation, testing and commissioning expertise for a major capital project in a neighboring country. The work is systems integration, coordinating with original equipment manufacturers and stakeholders, rather than a turnkey line built by one company alone.

What to Watch Next

Neither report gave a completion schedule or package-wise contract values, and those details will determine how the orders flow into L&T's revenue over the coming years. The next markers are execution milestones on CP09 and CP10, and whether DMTCL awards further Line 1 packages to the same group. For now, the facts established by both sources are clear: two packages, one repeat client, and a 31-kilometre underground line that will depend on L&T's systems to operate.
